title: Ramayana Passes Dhurandhar 2's 11-Day Worldwide Record, Tracker Estimates Show
excerpt: Sacnilk's updated tally puts Ramayana at an estimated ₹1,384.50 crore worldwide after 11 days, with India net at ₹760.60 crore — though the tracker figures are still being revised.
body:
• Ramayana has reached an estimated ₹1,384.50 crore worldwide after 11 days, according to trade tracker Sacnilk — passing Dhurandhar 2's 11-day worldwide mark of ₹1,354.92 crore.
  • India net collections stand at an estimated ₹760.60 crore after 11 days; overseas gross is an estimated ₹499.43 crore.
  • The film is now the seventh-highest-grossing Indian film ever, having passed KGF: Chapter 2's lifetime total on its tenth day, per Mint.
  • Box-office trackers' figures are estimates and are still being revised: Mint's early Sunday estimates ran lower, at ₹748.15 crore India net.

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana has passed another record. Trade tracker Sacnilk's updated tally puts the film at an estimated ₹1,384.50 crore worldwide after 11 days in cinemas — beyond the ₹1,354.92 crore that Dhurandhar 2 had collected worldwide at the same point, which had stood as the 11-day benchmark. India net collections are an estimated ₹760.60 crore, with overseas contributing an estimated ₹499.43 crore of the worldwide gross.

The second weekend did the heavy lifting. Sacnilk's day-by-day India net figures show ₹48.10 crore on the second Friday — itself a record second Friday, as The Videshi reported — jumping 51.6% to ₹72.90 crore on the second Saturday, split ₹53.75 crore from Hindi and ₹19.15 crore from the southern languages combined. The film, which stars Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi and was released in Hindi with dubbed versions in Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam and Kannada, had already crossed ₹1,000 crore worldwide in eight days, the third-fastest Indian film to get there.

Where it stands in the record books

Per Mint, the film passed the lifetime collection of KGF: Chapter 2 on its tenth day and is now the seventh-highest-grossing Indian film of all time, ahead of Jawan, Pathaan and Kalki 2898 AD. Domestically, its India net total is closing on RRR's lifetime ₹782.20 crore, with Dhurandhar's ₹840.20 crore the next mark above that. Ramayana is the first part of a two-part production mounted on a reported ₹4,000 crore budget across both films.

Read the numbers with care

These are tracker estimates, not audited figures, and they moved through Sunday: Mint's early Sunday estimates, also sourced from Sacnilk, put day 11 at ₹62.55 crore net and the India net total at ₹748.15 crore, before Sacnilk's later update lifted the worldwide total to ₹1,384.50 crore. The direction is not in dispute — the film has had an exceptional second weekend — but the exact record margins will settle as final tallies replace estimates.

What's next

The next test is the third weekend: whether Ramayana can hold screens against new releases and convert its record pace into a place among the very top lifetime grossers. Part Two is scheduled to follow in 2028.
